name: Tretinoin for beard

lead: Tretinoin is a prescription vitamin A derivative used on skin for acne and photoaging. In beard-growth forums it is sometimes mixed or layered with minoxidil on the theory that it improves absorption.
A general reference notes the evidence for tretinoin boosting minoxidil in hair loss is weak and contradictory, and no beard studies were found.

paras: Tretinoin binds retinoic acid receptors and normalizes follicle keratinization; the proposed minoxidil link is increased conversion of minoxidil to its active sulfate form.
Topical use commonly causes redness, peeling, irritation and sun sensitivity; oral tretinoin is contraindicated in pregnancy. It is prescription-only in the US, UK and EU.

lead: Tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) is a retinoid prescribed mainly for acne, and for photoaging; the oral form treats acute promyelocytic leukemia.[1] In some beard-growth routines it is combined with minoxidil, which is approved for scalp hair loss and used off-label for beard growth.[2]

Wikipedia reports tretinoin has been studied with minoxidil for hair loss, partly for its possible ability to increase minoxidil sulfate production, and describes the evidence as weak and contradictory.[1] No studies found on tretinoin for beard growth.

paras: In skin, tretinoin binds retinoic acid receptors and retinoid X receptors in keratinocytes, normalizing follicle keratinization and reducing inflammation signaling.[1] Minoxidil is a prodrug converted by sulfotransferase enzymes to minoxidil sulfate, which is the active form.[2]

Topical use can cause irritation, redness, peeling, blistering and increased sun sensitivity.[1] Oral tretinoin is contraindicated in pregnancy because of birth-defect risk; Australia rates the topical form category D.[1]

Tretinoin was patented in 1957 and approved for medical use in 1962; it was developed for acne at the University of Pennsylvania by James Fulton and Albert Kligman and FDA-approved for acne in 1971.[1] Minoxidil was named in 1963, introduced for hypertension in 1971, and approved topically for male baldness in 1988.[2]
No studies found for beard growth. A general reference describes studies of tretinoin plus minoxidil for scalp hair loss with weak and contradictory evidence.[1]

lore.intro: Tretinoin appears in beard forums as an add-on to minoxidil.

claims.claim: Adding tretinoin to minoxidil increases absorption and beard results.

timeline.event: Topical minoxidil approved for male baldness (Rogaine).[2]
